why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` matches the package.json script `node --test`, and the files index.js, README.md and test/strutil.test.js all exist at this commit. `node --input-type=module -e "..."` is valid Node usage. The README-heading script is the trickiest part, but it holds up. Inside bash double quotes, `\\\\` turns into `\\` and `\`` turns into a literal backtick. JS therefore receives `new RegExp('^#{1,6}\\s+`?' + f + '\\b')`, which is a valid regex. `'\n'` and `/^#{1,6}\s/` reach JS unchanged, and the script has no `$` for the shell to expand. The `!` in `!heads` would only trigger history expansion in an interactive shell, not when an agent runs the command. Checks 1 and 2 use valid assert/strict calls. The named import of padLeft fits once the builder adds the export, which an earlier step does.
